newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH YIELD CURVE STEEPER, BONDS TRACK BUNDS UP.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH YIELD CURVE STEEPER, BONDS TRACK BUNDS UP.

text.p: Markka bonds closed a shade
softer in calm trade in line with weaker bunds, dealers said.
The yield curve steepened slightly on profit taking in the
long end, going against the international trend towards flatter
curves, they said. The yield on the 2006 bond rose four basis
points on Friday's close to 5.84 bps.
Dealers said that some London houses had grown jittery on a
report in the Financial Times, saying that Finland would need
to revise its 1996 budget deficit due to a statistical error.
The report that said the 1996 deficit would be revised to
3.1 percent from 2.6 percent of GDP.
The finance ministry told Reuters Finland it is still
confident the 1997 public sector deficit would be within the
three percent limit for EMU, despite the 1996 overshoot.
"We have not changed our forecast for this year," state
secretary Raimo Sailas said, referring to the ministry's EMU
deficit forecast of 1.4 percent of GDP.
The international market had settled down to wait for
second-quarter U.S. employment cost data, due on Tuesday at
1530/1230 GMT, dealers said.
The markka was steady against the mark in late trade and
was seen in a 2.9500-2.9700 range near term, dealers said.
